newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
NEW ESTIMATE DOUBLES NUMBER OF INDIA'S POOR

A new method of estimating adopted by the government doubled the number of those recognised as poor to 320 million. In the new method, as much as 36 percent of the country's population falls below the poverty line. The prime minister, overruling objections to the new methodology by the finance and agriculture ministers, argued he could not go back on a commitment made to parliament while announcing the targeted public distribution system recently. By implication, the government recognised the need for a massive increase in the expenditure on various poverty alleviation and employment generation programmes.
Indian Express
PRESIDENT'S RULE EXTENSION IN UTTAR PRADESH CLEARED

The cabinet has cleared the extension of president's rule in Uttar Pradesh for a further six months, beginning on April 17, 1997. The lower house was expected to pass this extension on March 13. Sources said all major parties, including the Bharatiya Janata Party, agreed to the extension. Senior leaders of the ruling coalition said fresh assembly elections would be held after the extended term expired in October.
The Hindustan Times
UTTAR PRADESH GOVERNOR MAY BE RECALLED

The ruling United Front reconciled itself to recalling the Uttar Pradesh governor, if the Congress party made it a precondition for its support to defeat the Bharatiya Janata Party motion. The motion would be debated on March 20-21. From all available indications, the governor did not command much support within the ruling coalition, except the defence minister. The prime minister, as well as the two prominent Left parties, favoured his recall.
Business Standard
CEILING ON POLITICAL DONATIONS LIKELY TO STAY AT FIVE PCT

The threshold for political contributions in a year by a company may be retained at five percent of the average net profit. Though the report by the working group set up to recast the Companies Act, was silent on the issue, there were suggestions to make it mandatory for companies to make such contributions by cheque, with the shareholders' approval. Though the working group was unable to arrive at a consensus on the issue, in the coming meetings it was expected to incorporate the proposed changes in the draft bill being finalised.
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT TO MAKE INFORMATION A RIGHT

The government is planning to modify the existing local and administrative framework so that the disclosure of government information will be the rule and withholding it an exception. This move is in line with the suggestions of foreign and Indian corporates to make government functioning more transparent. As a first step, the Department of Personnel and Training has set up a working group on right to information and promotion of open and transparent government. It will study various suggestions to move towards the final objective of making the right to information a right for Indian citizens.
CABINET CLEARS CLUTCH OF FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROPOSALS

The Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment cleared Videsh Sanchar Nigam's $750 million global depository receipts issue. It also approved the proposal of Hindustan Petro Chemicals for a joint venture with Total of France to set up a liquefied natural gas terminal. A proposal for an increase in foreign equity participation in Tata Teleservices' project by Bell Canada to 49 percent was also approved. Among other approvals were Fiat's four-wheeler joint venture with the Doshi's and Daewoo's proposal for increasing stake in its joint venture with DCM to 49 percent.
ADVERSE OUTLOOK NOT TO CHANGE RATING: MOODY'S

The unfavourable economic outlook, mentioned in a Moody's outlook report on India, was not an indication of any attempt on the part of the U.S. credit rating agency to change the country's sovereign rating. An analyst at Moody's said this was an outlook for the short to mid-term and had no bearing on the credit rating. India's political environment, slowdown in economic growth and deterioration in its macroeconomic balances led Moody's to take an unfavourable outlook on the economic scenario in its report, leading to speculation of a change in the country's rating.
TATAS SHOW INTEREST IN GOVERNMENT'S HOTEL OUTFIT

The Tatas have shown an interest for a larger share in the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC), even as the government prepared to divest its holding in the hotel outfit. With ITDC's chain of hotels in prime metro areas shoring up high-value international business, the Tata's interest was not surprising. The Tatas own 10 percent of ITDC through the first tranche of divestment. However, the ITDC management has reportedly extracted an assurance from the tourism minister that the government would restrict its divestment to 49 percent for the moment. This was despite the disinvestment panel's recommendation to offload 79 percent stake in ITDC.
BUDGET'S SALIENT FEATURES TO STAY: STEERING PANEL

The crucial meeting of the ruling United Front coalition's steering panel gave strong pointers that there would be no major rollback on the salient features of the budget as outlined by the finance minister. This was despite severe objections voiced by the Front's Left constituents recently regarding some aspects of the budget, including disinvestment, tax exemptions and the opening up of the health insurance sector. Although the steering panel did not take up a detailed discussion on the budget as scheduled, party leaders indicated the issue would be amicably settled.
Financial Express
CRR TO BE CUT BELOW 10 PCT IN MEDIUM TERM

The Reserve Bank of India estimated inflation would be under control and in consonance with real output growth. It would use the cash reserve ratio (CRR) flexibly, but eventually cut it below 10 percent, the RBI governor said in an interview. Weak banks' recapitalisation needs would be met despite the absence of a provision for such funds in the budget, he added. The governor also hinted at abolishing the CRR on inter-bank borrowings and reimposition of CRR on deposits of non-resident Indians.
BZW UPGRADES CORPORATE EARNINGS

Foreign investment firms operating in Indian markets started revising their growth estimates, following the budget. Investment firm BZW Asia forecast a higher earnings growth for the corporate sector as a result of tax cuts and other reliefs. BZW was revising its corporate earnings growth for the year 1998 to 27 percent from 24 percent. In its report on the Budget, BZW expected across-the-board tax cuts and rationalisation to boost consumption and industrial growth, helping gross domestic product to grow at seven percent.
HPCL SEEKS PARTNER FOR WEST COAST REFINERY

Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) is searching for a new partner for its proposed west coast refinery in Maharashtra. If it failed to find a suitable one, the country's second largest oil company, might opt for going it alone. The rationale was that once commissioned, the proposed six million tonne per annum (MTPA) capacity refinery would provide HPCL an edge over its rivals in the western region in terms of installed capacity. The company already has a six MTPA refinery in Bombay and thus, its total refining capacity would go up to 12 MTPA.
Business Standard
NORMS FOR INVESTMENTS IN OVERRSEAS VENTURES EASED

The Reserve Bank of India relaxed provisions for Indian direct investment in joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries abroad under the fast track route (FTR). Now export earnings and other forex earnings will be considered for FTR clearance. The investment shall not exceed 25 percent of annual average export or foreign exchange earnings (other than equity exports) in the preceding three years, not exceeding $4 million. The five-year repatriation period will now be computed from the date of first remittance of equity, or of first shipment of equity exports, or the due date for receipt of entitlements from the foreign concern to be capitalised, whichever is earlier.
LEGAL HITCH STALLS INVESTMENT IN POWER, TELECOM

Investments in power and telecom projects would not be eligible for tax exemptions, although the budget contained provisions for 100 percent tax exemption to investors in the infrastructure sector. The scope of the relevant law was broadened by including telecom and power investments. However, the relevant sections of the act, which define the scope of infrastructure, was not amended. The norms require an infrastructure facility to be developed on a basis wherein ownership was passed on to the state after a specified period. But policy guidelines, announced recently for the power and telecom sectors, said projects would be taken up without any transfer clause.
The Observer
RULES OF ORIGIN A NON-TARIFF BARRIER

India criticised the United States for introducing the rules of origin in trading. The United States would now consider textile products, if exported to another country for printing or dying and re-exported by the second country, to have originated from the first country. Latest trade data revealed a decline in exports of made-ups in April-December 1996 as against the corresponding period in the previous fiscal. The textiles industry, however, feared the U.S. decision might encourage other developed countries to adopt the rules of origin, thereby affecting trade through the second country.
INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS ABANDON PROJECTS

The government's inability to supply naphtha to independent power producers (IPPs) forced them to abandon about 300 mini power projects. The decision was unofficially conveyed to the Power Ministry. Industry sources said the IPPs felt cheated because the government falsely promised them adequate supply of naphtha. The Power and the Petroleum Ministries had earlier promised adequate naphtha supplies, but later on backed off saying enough fuel was not available.
CEPA TO BUILD 3,960 MW POWER PROJECT

Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) of Taiwan was setting up a 3,960-megawatt coal-fired thermal power station in Orissa at a cost of $5.3 billion. The company formed a new subsidiary Consolidated Electric Power Asia (India) for the purpose. The project received a favourable responses from the Foreign Investment Promotion Board and the cabinet review committee. It was now awaiting clearance from the Central Electricity Authority.
